name: Login Admin
authorization_basis: OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0, published as a deliberately insecure application for security training; run locally, bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
request_summary: Login with email field set to an OR-true SQL comment payload and an arbitrary password. Payload masked here as <SQLI-OR-TRUE-COMMENT>.
root_cause_location: routes/login.ts:34 builds the query with a template string: SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}' ... The email is concatenated, not bound.
remediation: Use a parameterised query or the ORM's where-conditions so the email is passed as a bound value; never interpolate request input into SQL text. Validate and canonicalise the email before use.

name: View Basket
authorization_basis: OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0, deliberately insecure training application; local instance on 127.0.0.1 only; two synthetic lab accounts created on the disposable instance.
request_summary: Authenticated as synthetic user alice (own basket id 8), requested basket id 9 belonging to synthetic user bob. The session credential was held in memory only and is not stored here.
root_cause_location: routes/basket.ts:18-31 loads and returns the basket selected by req.params.id without checking that it belongs to the authenticated user. Lines 21-24 detect and score the training challenge; they do not enforce ownership.
root_cause_detail: The server keys the object on req.params.id and never confirms the basket belongs to the authenticated principal. This is an insecure direct object reference.
remediation: Derive the basket from the authenticated session (user.bid) rather than trusting the path id, or add a server-side ownership check that the basket's UserId equals the token subject before returning it.

name: Admin Section
authorization_basis: OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0, deliberately insecure training application; local instance on 127.0.0.1 only; admin session established locally via the same injection weakness proven in Login Admin.
request_summary: The administration UI route is protected only by a client-side Angular guard. Navigating to it in a local browser registers the challenge. The underlying data endpoint GET /api/Users returned 28 user records to a freshly-registered non-admin synthetic account, confirming the control is client-side only.
root_cause_location: frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:79-81 marks the 'administration' route with canActivate:[AdminGuard], a client-side check; the server exposes /api/Users without an equivalent role check.
remediation: Enforce authorization on the server for every admin data endpoint (role check on /api/Users and related routes). A client-side route guard is a usability aid, not an access control; it must never be the only gate.

name: API-only XSS
authorization_basis: OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0, deliberately insecure training application; local instance on 127.0.0.1 only; synthetic lab session.
request_summary: Persisted the official teaching payload, an iframe element whose src uses a script pseudo-scheme, into a product description through the REST API, bypassing the client form entirely. Payload masked here as <IFRAME-SCRIPT-SRC>.
root_cause_location: server.ts:389 leaves the authorization middleware for PUT /api/Products/:id commented out; the generated Product REST resource accepts the description update; and search-result/search-result.component.ts:109-113 renders every product description with DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml.
root_cause_detail: The product update endpoint accepts attacker-controlled description markup and the product-results component explicitly bypasses Angular's normal output sanitisation for that field. Together they make stored XSS reliable.
remediation: Layered fix: validate and reject markup on input; store raw and HTML-sanitise on output with an allowlist library (e.g. DOMPurify) instead of bypassSecurityTrustHtml; and add a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline script and script pseudo-scheme execution so a missed case cannot run.
